# Text, Numbers & Pickers

**Controls on show:** `text`, `textarea`, `number`, `color`, `date`.

**The one idea:** every input control is *bound* to a name via its `bind` field. When you change the control, the notebook bridge (`nb`) stores the new value under that name, and every downstream cell can read it with `nb.get('name')`. No wiring, no event handlers — just a shared bag of values.

Two things worth noticing as you play below:

- **Types matter.** A `number` control stores a real JavaScript `number`; a `text`/`color`/`date` control stores a `string`. The Live-values cell prints both the value **and** `typeof` so you can see it.
- **Live vs debounced.** The text and note fields don't write on *every* keystroke — they wait ~150 ms after you stop typing (a debounce), then commit. Colour and date commit when the picker closes. This keeps big notebooks from stuttering.

{
  "title": "Text, numbers & pickers",
  "description": "Type/pick a value and watch the Live-values cell report what each control wrote to nb — and its JavaScript type.",
  "width": 900,
  "height": 320,
  "controls": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "label": "Your name",
      "bind": "name",
      "default": "Ada",
      "placeholder": "type here…",
      "x": 0,
      "y": 0,
      "width": 280,
      "height": 64
    },
    {
      "type": "number",
      "label": "Age (clamped 0–120)",
      "bind": "age",
      "default": 36,
      "min": 0,
      "max": 120,
      "step": 1,
      "x": 300,
      "y": 0,
      "width": 280,
      "height": 64
    },
    {
      "type": "color",
      "label": "Favourite colour",
      "bind": "colour",
      "default": "#7c3aed",
      "x": 600,
      "y": 0,
      "width": 280,
      "height": 64
    },
    {
      "type": "date",
      "label": "A date",
      "bind": "day",
      "default": "1815-12-10",
      "x": 0,
      "y": 84,
      "width": 280,
      "height": 64
    },
    {
      "type": "textarea",
      "label": "A note (debounced)",
      "bind": "note",
      "default": "Bindings update live.",
      "rows": 3,
      "x": 300,
      "y": 84,
      "width": 580,
      "height": 120
    }
  ]
}

## Try this

- Type **999** into *Age* and click away — the Live-values cell shows `120`, because the `number` control clamps to its `max`. Now delete it entirely: it falls back to `min` (0), never a blank.
- Change *Your name* to `42` — the Live-values cell still reports `type: "string"`. Text boxes never guess numbers.
- Pick a new *Favourite colour*. Note the value is a 7-char hex string like `#00b894` — perfect for feeding an HTML cell later (see **Shape Studio**).
- Open the UI cell's editor (the pencil) and give the *note* field a `suffix`. Nothing happens — `suffix` only formats *readouts* and *sliders*, not text inputs. A good reminder that formatting is a display concern.
